messages:
Ant: Quick follow-up to the lease-allocator RFC — I hit a rollback race in staging when eviction overlaps lease-renew. Repro is small-batch, non-deterministic but frequent under load.
Sel: Ugh. I saw a one-off like that yesterday too. Thought it was eviction timing. Can you paste the logs?
Ant: gist of logs:
```
[evict] lease=123 renew@1761111110 -> rollback
[kv] free page=0x7fabc still referenced
[compact] removed slab slot 42
```
Sel: That looks like renew ack wasn't visible to the compactor before it reclaimed the slot.
Jia: Sounds like a visibility/ordering problem between lease persistence and compactor notifications. Current flow: allocate -> persist lease -> notify evictor/compactor. If notify is delayed or async ack lost, compactor may operate on stale state.
Tom: We have three broad fixes: 1) make persist+notify synchronous (latency hit), 2) introduce monotonic lease-gen with CAS semantics to make evict idempotent, 3) compactor consults authoritative lease table before reclaim (extra RPCs).
Ant: I sketched option 2 in the RFC thread earlier but didn't nail edge cases. Sketch: each lease carries (tenant, gen). Renew increments gen and writes. Evict reads lease.gen and only reclaims if the gen matches the expected free token.
Sel: That reduces windows but requires the gen write to be linearizable or use a CAS on the metadata store. If writes can be reordered, we still lose.
Jia: CAS on metadata store is possible but increases pressure. Alternative: allow spurious aborts (compactor backs off) — easier on infra, slightly more CPU. We should evaluate abort rate vs added RPC latency.
Tom: I like the gen+CAS compromise: low-latency common case, strong guard on races. If CAS fails, compactor retries/backoff.
Ant: Mini-proof sketch for the compare step:
```
// on renew
old = read(lease_key)
new = old.gen + 1
write_with_cas(lease_key, old, new)
// on evict
cur = read(lease_key)
if cur.gen == expected_free_gen: reclaim else abort
```
Sel: Two practical checks: (A) are our metadata KV stores offering CAS? (B) what's the steady-state retry amplification? If both OK, implement.
Jia: For (A) Vault/KV provider in Dedicated/Private path supports CAS via etcd-style compare. Hosted will need a shim to the global metadata service. I'll audit providers tomorrow.
Tom: I'll prototype the cas path in the allocator branch and add a microbenchmark for renew+evict concurrency.
Ant: Also: add three telemetry counters: lease_reclaim_abort, lease_double_ref_detect, lease_cas_fail_rate. Want to see how often compactor aborts vs truly free slots.
ops-bot: feature-flagging: deploy/lease-metrics toggled ON in staging (flag: lease_metrics_v1).
Sel: I'll hook the counters into the evictor and compact pipeline, and add a unit test that injects a renew-delay to force the race.
Jia: I'll open an issue linking the original RFC #421 and list perf targets: 99p latency increase < 1ms, abort rate < 0.1% under normal load.
Ant: Other tradeoffs to call out in the write-up: increased metadata ops vs fewer correctness incidents; complexity of CAS shim for hosted; possible need for batching lease-gen increments to reduce metadata QPS.
Tom: If we batch increments per-tenant, we need to ensure ordering/generation monotonicity across workers. Slightly tricky but doable. I'll note it in the prototype.
Sel: Good plan. Let's keep the synchronous persist option on the table in case CAS path proves noisy.
Jia: Cool. Action items: Tom -> prototype CAS path (+bench); Sel -> telemetry + race test; Jia -> audit metadata providers + open issue; Ant -> update RFC with this follow-up and add metrics list. Check-in Friday. :thumbsup:
Tom: I'll start today.
Ant: Thanks all.
thread_summary: Follow-up on lease-allocator RFC: rollback race between eviction and lease-renew. Discussed options (sync persist, gen+CAS, authoritative RPC), decided to prototype gen+CAS with telemetry and tests. Action items assigned.
